A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same paper, Knee-Deep in C-RASP: A Transformer Depth Hierarchy, with complete main text and Appendices A–G. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer training and evaluation on synthetic sequential-dependency languages, including next-token prediction and length-generalization accuracies in Section 5 and Figures 2 and 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and accuracy results in Section 5 and Figures 2 and 4.

M1.justification: The fixed-precision transformer definition, attention-rounding procedure, logic constructions, positional-encoding extensions, and experimental training objective remain unchanged (Sections 2–3 and 5; Appendices B and F).

E1.justification: Both evaluate next-token prediction on the same synthetic L_3 through L_12 languages and sequence-length bins from 201–250 through 351–400. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The experiments retain the same transformer depth comparisons. Neither version evaluates additional external baseline methods; the introduction's comparison with prior theoretical work is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same sampling procedure, 800/200 training-validation split, model dimensions, learning-rate search, 25-epoch stopping rule, and whole-sequence accuracy criterion.

E4.justification: The analyses of depth dependence and length generalization in Section 5 and Figure 4 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point accuracies without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All accuracy entries in Figures 2 and 4 match, as do the findings in Section 5.3. For example, depth-10 accuracy on L_12 at lengths 351–400 remains 62%.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, and proofs remain unchanged, including Theorem 3.1, Theorems 4.10–4.12, and Corollary 5.2. Appendices A–F are identical in extracted text and rendered appearance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same depth-preserving equivalence, strict depth-hierarchy claims, positional-encoding extensions, and empirical alignment claim. The revised opening captions restate existing claims.

C2.justification: Sections 5.3 and 6 retain the same interpretations and qualifications concerning width, data diversity, training dynamics, the fixed-precision definition, omitted positional-encoding experiments, and restriction to formal-language tasks.

D1.justification: Implementation, hyperparameter, GPU-resource, and computational-cost disclosures remain unchanged. The code-access link and LLM-assistance disclosure move from page 9 to page 8 without changing their content.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the introduction's comparison of earlier transformer depth-separation results. The reference pages are identical.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the captions to Figures 1 and 2 and changes appendix cross-references from 'Section' to 'Appendix,' including in the notation index. These are limited editorial changes; section order and narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: The opening figure captions are shortened, spacing changes, and the conference notice moves from page 2 to page 1, accompanied by main-text reflow. Existing diagrams, heatmaps, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides modest caption and cross-reference polish, with accompanying layout shifts. The theoretical arguments, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations are unchanged, leaving the paper's overall quality essentially the same.
